proposal.blind_spot: The optimizer sees L1 and DRAM utilization but cannot tell whether L2 is the true saturated memory unit, and cannot tell whether the mediocre occupancy is register-limited (fixable) or not.

rationale.lts__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustaine: HIGH (>= dram__throughput) -> L2 is the real bottleneck: cut L2 request traffic via 128-bit vectorized accesses, cache-modifier hints, and block swizzling for locality / LOW (<< dram) -> DRAM bytes are the only lever: fuse stages, downcast dtypes, avoid materializing intermediates.
rationale.launch__occupancy_limit_registers: HIGH-binding -> register pressure caps the 51-66% occupancy: shrink BLOCK_SIZE and reduce live values to add warps that hide long-scoreboard stalls / LOW -> occupancy is limited elsewhere: change block size or grid mapping instead and do not sacrifice register-heavy tiling.

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:It uses portable percent-of-peak utilization cuts for high-DRAM versus L1-active regimes with all quadrants populated, unlike workload-size absolute bytes/register-count cuts or the empty-branch extreme split.
